name: Palma de Mallorca Airport

runway.v: two runways; the longest, 06L/24R, is 3,270 m long and 45 m wide

slots.v: a slot request counts as not authorised until confirmed coordination is received
slots.quote: The slot request shall be understood as not authorized until the reception of the confirmed coordination.

handling.v: a handling agent is mandatory for all general and business aviation; the AIP lists Aviapartner Palma de Mallorca FBO and Mallorcair as authorised FBOs
handling.quote: It is mandatory to contract handling agent for all operation to General and Business Aviation

max_aircraft.v: aircraft over 20 m long may park on the general aviation apron for at most 7 days
max_aircraft.quote: the maximum parking time on the general aviation apron for an aircraft over 20 m in length shall be 7 days

noise.v: at night (summer 2100-0500, winter 2200-0600) no training flights, no APU use and no reverse thrust above idle except for safety
noise.quote: The term night hours is defined as the time period comprised between: V: 2100-0500, I: 2200-0600.

notes: Source is the ENAIRE AIP amendment page for AD 2 LEPA/LESJ dated 03-SEP-26 (Amdt 2026/410); the current consolidated AD 2 page could not be opened. Night hours are given without UTC/LT marking (Spanish AIP normally uses UTC; if UTC both seasons equal 23:00-07:00 local) - not converted. The night rules restrict training, APU and reverse thrust; no ban on movements was found, but absence is not stated, so curfew is left missing. Footnote (1) on hours: foreign state/military aircraft need PPR 72 h ahead (not relevant to charter). GA ramp agents also listed: Aviapartner, General Aviation Service, Gestair, Jetland Executive Services, Mallorcair, Melendez, Sky Valet Spain. Re-researched 2026-10-29: Re-read Amdt 2026/410 AD 2 LEPA: AD 2.20 and AD 2.21 contain no ban on night movements and no PPR for general or business aviation (PPR 72 hours is only for foreign state aircraft). The night-hours times (V: 2100-0500, I: 2200-0600) carry no UTC/LT label, while the same page marks local times explicitly as 'LT' elsewhere (e.g. 'HR 0730-1430 LT'); this suggests the unmarked times are UTC but the AIP section does not say so. Also in AD 2.20: from 1 May to 31 October, aircraft cruising slower than 220 kt are restricted 0530-0700 and 1600-1830 (no time label).
